claims.claim: Williams states that detection tools are not reading and not evaluating authorial intent but measuring two mathematical properties of text, perplexity and burstiness.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor of The New Publishing Standard, 2026

verdicts.trueWording: They are not reading. They are not evaluating authorial intent, creative decision-making, or the presence of a human mind in the work. They are measuring two mathematical properties of text.
verdicts.note: Raw HTML fetched with a browser UA (HTTP 200, 26451 bytes) and stripped to text; the live page was reached directly, no summarizer or archive needed. Quote 'They are not reading.' appears word for word under the heading 'How The Tools Actually Work - And Why They Fail'. Every limb holds: not reading; not evaluating authorial intent; 'measuring two mathematical properties of text'; 'The first is perplexity - how statistically surprising each word choice is'; 'The second is burstiness ... it measures variation in sentence length and complexity'. Byline is Mark Williams, dated Jun 9, 2026. The source-field descriptor 'editor of The New Publishing Standard' is not asserted on the page itself (the word 'editor' there refers to David Shelley), but that descriptor is not a limb of the claim sentence.
